findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/SpecialLinearGroup.lean:225 `def map (f : R →+* S) : SpecialLinearGroup n R →* SpecialLinearGroup n S`; the transvection section there is `variable {ι F : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] [CommRing F]`. The proof body here is `simp only [... map_add]; split_ifs <;> simp_all` — no `Algebra` use. Compare `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Transvection.lean:242 map_transvectionUnit (f : A →+* B)`, which already has the general signature.
findings.fix: State it at the natural level next to the existing `TauCeti.map_transvectionUnit`: `theorem map_transvection {n} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] (f : A →+* B) (hij : i ≠ j) (c : A) : SpecialLinearGroup.map f (transvection hij c) = transvection hij (f c)`, and apply it here as `map_transvection φ.toRingHom`.
findings.issue: `map_transvection` assumes `φ : A →ₐ[R] B` and fixes the index type to `Fin N`, but the proof uses only `map_add` and passes `φ.toRingHom` to `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map`, which takes a `R →+* S`. The `R`-algebra structure and the `Fin N` restriction are unused.

findings.evidence: TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Transvection.lean:178 `def transvectionHom (hij : i ≠ j) : Multiplicative A →* GL n A` with `variable {n : Type*} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n]`; line 141 `def transvectionUnit hij c := SpecialLinearGroup.toGL (SpecialLinearGroup.transvection hij c)`; Mathlib states `SpecialLinearGroup.transvection` for arbitrary `[DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι]`.
findings.fix: Hoist it to the matrix level with `{n} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n]` as a public `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup`-valued one-parameter subgroup, and redefine `TauCeti.transvectionHom` (and its `map_one'`/`map_mul'` proofs) as its composite with `SpecialLinearGroup.toGL`.
findings.issue: `transvectionHom : Multiplicative A →* SL (Fin N) A` is a special case (index type `Fin N`, private) of a fact already proved publicly at arbitrary index type for `GL n A`, and the general SL statement is what the GL one should be derived from: `TauCeti.transvectionHom = SpecialLinearGroup.toGL ∘ (SL transvectionHom)` definitionally, since `transvectionUnit hij c = toGL (SpecialLinearGroup.transvection hij c)`.

findings.evidence: This file lines 113-114 `simpa [Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection_coe, Matrix.one_apply, Matrix.single_apply, hij] using hentry` versus TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Transvection.lean:191-195 `transvectionUnit_injective ... simpa [transvection, Matrix.one_apply, Matrix.single_apply, hij] using congrFun₂ h' i j`, which GeneralLinear/RootSubgroup.lean:116 uses directly.
findings.fix: Add `SpecialLinearGroup.transvection` injectivity at the matrix level (general index type) next to `transvectionUnit_injective`, derive `transvectionUnit_injective` from it via injectivity of `toGL`, and use it here in place of the inline `simpa [transvection_coe, one_apply, single_apply, hij]`.
findings.issue: `rootSubgroupPoints_injective` re-proves the `(i,j)`-entry extraction for `SpecialLinearGroup.transvection` inline, duplicating the same computation already proved at arbitrary index type in `transvectionUnit_injective`; the GL analogue of this theorem just cites that lemma.

findings.evidence: Proof body lines 268-278: `sourcePresentation.surjective`, `sourceSchemePoints.symm.injective`, `symm_apply_apply` — all available for `Equiv`. Its only users are GeneralLinear/RootSubgroup.lean:241 and SpecialLinear/RootSubgroup.lean:301.
findings.fix: State it with `≃` (`Equiv`) throughout and drop the six `Group` instances; the two call sites pass `MulEquiv` arguments via `.toEquiv`.
findings.issue: `transportPointwiseFormula` requires `[Group P] [Group Q] [Group S] [Group T] [Group X] [Group Y]` and six `≃*`, but its proof uses only `surjective`, `symm_apply_apply` and `injective`; multiplicativity is never used (the three maps `mapPresentation`/`mapPoints`/`mapConcrete` are already bare functions). The group hypotheses are visibly unused and make the interface look like a homomorphism-transport lemma when it is pure bijection bookkeeping.

summary: Three matrix-level facts about `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection` are proved inside the `Fin N` group-scheme file with hypotheses stronger than their proofs need (`A →ₐ[R] B` instead of `A →+* B`, `Fin N` instead of an arbitrary index type), duplicating the existing general-index GL transvection API; and `transportPointwiseFormula` carries six unused `Group` instances and six `≃*` where the proof only uses `Equiv`.
